concerns.text: The primary statistical comparison (FR‑005) uses an exact McNemar test on paired binary success outcomes of the Symbolic approach versus the original Neural Policy baseline. However, these outcomes conflate planner feasibility with low‑level controller performance, because the Symbolic pipeline’s success is measured after real‑world execution (including controller failures), while the Neural Policy baseline’s success is also measured after real‑world execution. This design does not isolate the effect of topological symbolic abstraction from the effect of continuous physics fidelity, violating the core research question and Principle VI (Simulation Fidelity Independence). As a result, the test cannot attribute differences in success rates to the presence or absence of physics simulation, making the claimed conclusion about “topological constraints versus continuous dynamics” empirically unsupported.
